walking_notes: All four sit within about 250 ft of each other around the Hartz Ave & Church St intersection (OSM intersection node 37.820604, -121.998233). Hartz Ave runs NW–SE through downtown; odd numbers (Incontro 455, Rancho 501) are on the southwest side, even numbers (Kaia's 480, Harvest 500) on the northeast side. Church St crosses Hartz here (running SW to Railroad Ave and NE toward Front St / Bridges). Layout by quadrant: Rancho Cantina occupies the corner building south of Church on the SW side (DanvilleSanRamon: 'southeast corner of Hartz Avenue and Church Street'); Danville Harvest is directly across Hartz from Rancho, south of Church on the NE side (about 120 ft / one crosswalk apart); Kaia's is on Harvest's side of Hartz, roughly 110 ft northwest of the intersection (across Church St from Harvest, ~160 ft door to door); Incontro is on Rancho's side, about 170 ft northwest of the intersection (across Church St from Rancho, ~220 ft; 485 Hartz/New Moon Massage sits between Incontro and the corner). Pairwise distances (building centroids): Rancho–Harvest ~120 ft, Kaia's–Harvest ~160 ft, Incontro–Kaia's ~155 ft, Rancho–Kaia's ~215 ft, Rancho–Incontro ~220 ft, Incontro–Harvest ~250 ft — every pairing is under a one-minute walk with at most one street crossing. The Hartz/Church intersection was the first phase (April 2024) of the Town's $4.9M Downtown Master Plan Catalyst Project, which added enhanced pedestrian crossings, traffic-calming bulb-outs and new lighting at five Hartz intersections from School St to Linda Mesa Ave, so the crossing between Rancho and Harvest is a rebuilt pedestrian crossing. Church St and School St are 2-hour street parking; Hartz Ave is mostly 2-hour with loading zones (Town parking map). Nearest lots: Village Theatre Municipal Lot ~340 ft NE via Church St; Front Street Municipal Lot ~420 ft; Railroad Ave Municipal Lot ~440 ft SW via Church St (backs onto the Iron Horse Trail, which passes ~40 ft from Railroad & Church). Upscale neighbors inside the same pocket: Bridges Restaurant & Bar at 44 Church St (~230 ft NE of the corner) and Crush'd Wine Bar + Kitchen at 312 Railroad Ave (~210 ft SW).
neighborhood_description: The four restaurants anchor the quieter southern end of Danville's historic Hartz Avenue, one block north of where Hartz meets San Ramon Valley Blvd/Hartz Way and a two-to-three-minute walk south of the busier Prospect Ave/Danville Hotel/Prospect Park Plaza core. This stretch is where Danville's late-1800s/early-1900s residences were converted into restaurants: Incontro occupies the c.1910 Hartz House (home of John Hartz, the subdivider who created Hartz Avenue), Harvest the c.1903 Eddy House, and further south sit the Cabral House (551), Bret Read House (571) and Shuey/Podva House (100 School St) from the Town's Historic Downtown Walking Tour. Bay Area Telegraph calls the Hartz/Church corner 'one of downtown Danville's busiest restaurant stretches'; the Town's Catalyst Project (2024–25) rebuilt the intersection with bulb-outs, enhanced crossings and new light poles/lit bollards. Within ~250 ft are Bridges Restaurant & Bar (44 Church St, the Mrs. Doubtfire restaurant) and Crush'd Wine Bar + Kitchen (312 Railroad Ave, 24 wines on tap); the Village Theatre & Art Gallery (233 Front St, the 1874 Grange Hall) is ~315 ft NE; the Iron Horse Trail and the Railroad Ave lot (Saturday Farmers' Market) are one short block SW via Church St. The Town's official 'Live Locally' branding, the oak-tree logo and the 350-year-old Old Oak Tree (Diablo Rd, ~980 ft NE) frame the local identity. Compared with the north-Hartz/Prospect block (dive bar, music club, piano bar, brewery), this pocket is dinner-and-patio oriented: wood-fired Californio Mexican (Rancho, opened Aug 24, 2026), regional Italian in a historic house (Incontro, closed Mondays), farm-to-table (Harvest, dinner ends 8:30 pm daily) and Hawaiian/tiki cocktails with live Hawaiian music (Kaia's, bar to 11 pm Fri–Sat). Hours as read Sept 10, 2026 — Rancho Sun–Thu 11–10, Fri–Sat 11–11; Incontro dinner Tue–Thu & Sun 5–9, Fri–Sat 5–10, brunch buffet Sat 12–3 / Sun 10–2; Kaia's Sun–Tue 11:30–9, Wed–Thu 11:30–10, Fri–Sat 11:30–11 (kitchen closes an hour before the bar); Harvest lunch weekdays 11:30–3, brunch weekends 10–3, dinner daily 4–8:30, happy hour 3–5.

landmarks.name: Village Theatre & Art Gallery
landmarks.note: 233 Front St, Danville, CA 94526; (925) 314-3418. Built 1874 as the Grange Hall (Colonial Revival), raised in 1913 to become the second floor of a fraternal/social club; the Grange started Danville's first public library and high school. Town-owned theater + art gallery (gallery hours Wed–Fri 12–5, Sat 11–3 per Town page; offices M–Th 8–5, F 8–1). ~315 ft / 1–2 min NE of the corner via Church St. Adjacent Village Theatre Municipal Lot has 2-hr and 4-hr sections with EV charging.

Castle Companies' 2015–16 redevelopment preserved the hotel and McCauley House (dedicated town heritage resources 2016) and added ~35,000–37,500 sq ft of retail/restaurant space plus 16 second-floor residences at Hartz & W Prospect. ~380 ft / 1–2 min NW of the corner.

competitor_nightlife_zone.description: This is where Danville's late-night, music and bar energy concentrates: a 1907 dive bar, a live-music/DJ/karaoke club, a cocktail lounge open to midnight, a neighborhood sports bar with 25 taps and patio people-watching, the town's brewery, and (until recently) a dueling-piano bar and a DJ sports bar that ran until 1 am. Danville Social's 'Weekend Music Scene' lists DJs on Thursdays, bands Friday/Saturday and karaoke Sundays on this block. Two of the loudest venues have closed since early 2026 (Kick N Mule at 340 Hartz; Stilettos Piano Bar, ex-McGah's, at 148 E Prospect per Yelp listings and a dead website), so the block is in flux. South of Hartz, by contrast, is dinner-led: no DJs, live Hawaiian music at Kaia's, and most kitchens closing 8:30–10 pm.

town_facts: Town of Danville, Contra Costa County (East Bay), 'Heart of the San Ramon Valley'; ~30 miles east of San Francisco. Population 43,582 (2020 Census, Wikipedia) / 'approximately 43,146' (Town Community Profile); 18 sq mi; incorporated July 1, 1982 and one of the few California municipalities styled 'Town'. Founded 1854 by brothers Daniel and Andrew Inman on 400 acres bought with Gold Rush earnings; named Danville by 1858; post office 1860. The Southern Pacific branch line arrived June 7, 1891; John Hartz gave/sold 8.65 acres for the depot and subdivided 74 lots east of it, shifting commerce from Front St to the new Hartz Avenue; the Danville Hotel was turned to face Hartz in 1927. Wealthy, family-oriented suburb: Wikipedia cites ZIP 94506 as the 14th-wealthiest in America and the town as 2nd-highest-income U.S. place with 40,000+ residents. SafeWise named Danville California's safest city for 2026 (No. 1 six of the past nine years; violent crime 0.6 and property crime 5.9 per 1,000) — Town news release Feb 12, 2026. Town copy describes 'the perfect blend of upscale amenities and small-town charm', a 'quaint character', highly rated schools, year-round farmers' markets and street fairs, and a historic downtown of shops, restaurants and galleries 'from upscale eateries to family-friendly pizzerias'. Official brand since 2017: 'Live Locally' with an oak-tree logo (#LiveLocallyDanville); the 350-year-old Old Oak Tree on Diablo Rd is the town symbol and mascot Auggie the Acorn's home. Downtown investment: $4.9M Downtown Master Plan Catalyst Project (begun April 2024 at Hartz & Church) rebuilt five Hartz intersections from School St to Linda Mesa with raised/bulb-out crossings, lit bollards and new light poles; Prospect Park Plaza reopened July 2025 with a stage and oak sculptures; a new Town Green Pavilion starts construction Aug 2026 (done Spring 2027). What closes early (as read Sept 10, 2026): Museum of the SRV by 4 pm; Danville Harvest dinner ends 8:30 pm daily; Bridges dinner ends 8 pm Sun–Thu / 9 pm Fri–Sat; Danville Brewing bar 9 pm (9:30 Fri–Sat); Incontro 9 pm Tue–Thu & Sun, 10 pm Fri–Sat (closed Mondays); Crush'd 9 pm (10 Thu–Sat); Kaia's 9 pm Sun–Tue, 10 Wed–Thu, 11 Fri–Sat; Rancho Cantina 10 pm (11 Fri–Sat); Revel and Norm's 10–11 pm; Auburn Lounge is the late option at midnight nightly. The two 1-am venues (Kick N Mule, Stilettos) are listed closed. Farmers' Market Saturdays 9–1; Town offices M–Th 8–5, F 8–1. Downtown parking is free (1,400+ public spaces, six municipal lots), which the Town and press consistently highlight.

notes: Scope and caveats: (1) Coordinates are OpenStreetMap building/POI centroids retrieved via Overpass and Nominatim on Sept 10, 2026 (±10–20 m); the corner coordinate is the actual OSM street-intersection node of Hartz Ave and Church St. Distances are straight-line haversine values, so real walking paths are slightly longer. (2) Addresses were read from each restaurant's own website (ranchocantina.com/danville, incontrodanville.com, kaiasdanville.com, danvilleharvest.com/contact). Rancho Cantina's phone on its site is (925) 718-5153; a search summary showed (925) 519-3851 — use the site's. Rancho's soft-open date: Bay Area Telegraph says Monday Aug 24, 2026 (reservations Sep 1); Diablo Dish says 'Monday, August 26' (Aug 26, 2026 is a Wednesday, so likely a typo). (3) Hours are as read on Sept 10, 2026 and should be re-verified before publishing. (4) Parking time limits were read visually from the Town's color-coded Downtown Public Parking Map PDF (DocumentCenter/View/2427): orange = 3 hr (Clock Tower, Front Street, Rose Street), blue = 4 hr (Library/CC; parts of Village Theatre and Railroad lots), green = 2 hr (parts of Village Theatre and Railroad lots; most streets), dark green = 72 hr (Sycamore Valley Park & Ride). Lot capacities are not published except OSM's 82 for the Library lot. Sycamore Valley Park & Ride was not geocoded. (5) Village Theatre history (1874 Grange Hall) is from the Town's Historic Downtown Walking Tour Guide PDF; a search snippet of a Town page said 1873 and a 1,000 sq ft gallery opened Nov 14, 2009 — that page's text was not read directly. (6) Nightlife closures: Kick N Mule (340 Hartz) and Stilettos Piano Bar (148 E Prospect, ex-McGah's) appear as 'CLOSED' in Yelp listing titles surfaced by search (Feb and Aug 2026 respectively) and stilettosdanville.com does not resolve; no replacement tenant was found for 340 Hartz. Treat both as closed-pending-verification. (7) Not found / empty: 2026 dates for Lighting of the Old Oak Tree, Oktoberfest Danville and Danville Fallfest (the Chamber's Oct 2026 calendar shows neither Oktoberfest nor Fallfest; danvillefallfest.com is parked). 'Evenings in Danville' and discoverdowntowndanville.org in search results belong to Danville, INDIANA — excluded. (8) EBParks Iron Horse page and SFGate's Hartz Ave article returned 403/blank; Instagram profiles could not be read, so @discoverdanville ownership and @eastbayeats follower count are unverified; #LiveLocallyDanville is confirmed via the Town's 2017 Nextdoor branding post and LinkedIn. (9) The Danville Hotel's current tenants are not listed on the owner's page; OSM shows Basque Boulangerie Café there (unverified). (10) Oak Hill Park is ~1.6 mi north of downtown — not a walkable landmark for the district. (11) No prices or dishes were recorded beyond concept descriptions quoted from the restaurants' own sites and press.
